**Issue #1997 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #1997: Patch: the rules tests' act, live and one-effect runner come from the shared harness, and the check keeps it so
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

The engine's rule tests run to about 250 files, and many of them open by writing their own copy of the same few helpers: one to send an action, one to look up a card on the field, one to run a single effect. That comes to over a thousand lines, written again in about twenty slightly different shapes, and each new test file adds one more. After this, those helpers live once in the shared test harness, and the repository's check refuses a new copy, as it already does for the helpers moved in #1978. Players notice nothing. The maintainer and the bot get shorter, uniform tests.

## Why

Counted with `git grep` in `crates/engine/tests/rules`:

- 63 files declare their own `static NONCE` counter.
- There are 61 `fn act(` definitions, 40 `fn live(` and 18 `fn id_at`. Several of the `id_at` copies are exactly `unit_at(..).id`, which #1978 already shares.
- 144 files call `EngineSink::new(`. The survey found 31 of them hand-writing the same one-effect runner, about 18 lines each.
- Homes already compete: `fixtures/prompt_harness.rs:161` and `fixtures/mb22.rs:458` each have an `act` on a thread-local nonce. `fixtures/harness.rs` has neither, and `fixtures/credit.rs:229`, `damage_combat.rs:1044` and `field.rs:519` hold more.
- The copying continues after #1978. The Marketplace (#1963) added `run` (`marketplace.rs:51`), `NONCE` (`:107`) and `deal` (`:109`).
- #1978's `SHARED_TEST_HELPERS` (`crates/tools/tests/acceptance.rs:980`) holds none of these names.

## Proposal

- Put in `fixtures/harness.rs`:
  - one thread-local nonce counter, as `prompt_harness` and `mb22` already have, which keeps each test's nonces deterministic;
  - `act`, `act_result`, `live`, `live_mut` and `run_effect(state, effect, controller) -> Vec<GameEvent>`.
- Migrate the copies, and rename any helper whose body really differs.
- Add the names to the harness row of `SHARED_TEST_HELPERS`, and refuse a nonce static outside the harness.
- It can land in two parts: the action wrappers and nonce, then `live`, `live_mut` and `run_effect`.

## Where it lands

- `crates/engine/tests/rules/fixtures/harness.rs` and the rule test files that hold copies
- `crates/tools/tests/acceptance.rs`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-engine --features testkit --test rules` is green with the same number of tests before and after, both stated in the pull request.
- [ ] The acceptance scan finds no copy of those names outside the harness, and its scratch test refuses a planted copy of each and a planted `NONCE`.
- [ ] The diff touches only `crates/engine/tests/` and `crates/tools/tests/`.

## Size and risks

Hard by rule 11 for its file count (about 130 files), and mechanical: net about −1,300 lines. A test that relied on exact nonce values or on event order must keep them. It conflicts with any open pull request that adds rule tests, so it lands between them, or in its two parts.

---

```rust
thread_local! {
    /// The rules tests' one nonce counter (#1997). libtest runs each test on a thread of its own, so a
    /// test's nonces count `act-1`, `act-2`, … on every run.
    static NONCE: Cell<u32> = const { Cell::new(0) };
}

/// The calling test's next nonce: fresh within the test, so `reduce`'s dedupe (§9.3) never hands back
/// an earlier action's result in place of this one.
pub fn next_nonce() -> String {
    NONCE.with(|count| {
        count.set(count.get() + 1);
        format!("act-{}", count.get())
    })
}

/// `body` as an action with the next nonce. `body` is an `ActionInput` or its JSON literal, `playerId`
/// included; a nonce it carries is replaced.
pub fn next_action(body: impl Serialize) -> Action {
    json_as::<ActionInput>(json_of(body)).with_nonce(next_nonce())
}

/// `reduce` with the next nonce; a refusal comes back in the result.
pub fn act_result(state: &GameState, body: impl Serialize) -> ReduceResult {
    reduce(state, &next_action(body))
}

/// `act_result` for an action that must be accepted: a refusal panics with the action's type and reason.
pub fn act_ok(state: &GameState, body: impl Serialize) -> ReduceResult {
    let action = next_action(body);
    accepted(&action, reduce(state, &action))
}

/// `act_ok`'s state.
pub fn act(state: &GameState, body: impl Serialize) -> GameState {
    act_ok(state, body).state
}

/// `act_ok`, the action appended to `log`, for a test that replays what it played (§9.2).
pub fn act_logged(state: &GameState, body: impl Serialize, log: &mut Vec<Action>) -> ReduceResult {
    let action = next_action(body);
    let result = accepted(&action, reduce(state, &action));
    log.push(action);
    result
}

/// `act` with the nonce given, so two copies of one state sent the same action stay equal, `applied`
/// and all.
pub fn act_with_nonce(state: &GameState, body: impl Serialize, nonce: &str) -> GameState {
    let action = json_as::<ActionInput>(json_of(body)).with_nonce(nonce);
    accepted(&action, reduce(state, &action)).state
}

fn accepted(action: &Action, result: ReduceResult) -> ReduceResult {
    if let Some(error) = &result.error {
        panic!("{} refused: {error}", action.action_type());
    }
    result
}
```

```rust
/// The 1-based lines of `text` that declare a static named one of `statics` (`static NONCE: AtomicU32 = …`,
/// `pub static NONCE`, one inside a `thread_local!`), a `//` comment aside.
fn shared_static_declarations(text: &str, statics: &[&str]) -> Vec<usize> {
    text.lines()
        .enumerate()
        .filter(|(_, line)| {
            let code: Vec<&str> = line.split("//").next().unwrap_or("").split_whitespace().collect();
            code.windows(2).any(|pair| {
                pair[0] == "static" && statics.iter().any(|name| pair[1].strip_suffix(':') == Some(*name))
            })
        })
        .map(|(index, _)| index + 1)
        .collect()
}
```

    assert_eq!(shared_static_declarations(text, &["NONCE"]), [1, 3, 5]);

```rust
/// The card as it stands in `state` now, by its id or a copy of it (TS held the live object).
pub fn live(state: &GameState, card: impl Into<CardRef>) -> CardInstance {
    let id = ref_id(card.into());
    find_instance(state, &id)
        .cloned()
        .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("no card {id} in the state"))
}

/// The card in `state`, by its id or a copy of it, to write through (TS wrote the live object).
pub fn live_mut(state: &mut GameState, card: impl Into<CardRef>) -> &mut CardInstance {
    let id = ref_id(card.into());
    find_instance_mut(state, &id).unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("no card {id} in the state"))
}

fn ref_id(card: CardRef) -> String {
    match card {
        CardRef::Text(id) | CardRef::Instance { id, .. } => id,
    }
}
```
````
